In the context of a single-party framework agreement, the successful framework member does not have to compete for each new contract. It is emphasised that a framework agreement constitutes no guarantee to purchase a specific quantity of services from a particular economic operator. Indeed, the Contracting Authority reserves the right to operate outside of the framework agreement at its discretion, particularly should it become apparent that doing so would offer greater value for money. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Contracting Authority has adopted a framework agreement approach to the procurement of the required services in order to leverage efficiencies and maximise cost savings over a four (4)year period. Frequency and Time Reference Distribution Amplifiers The DIFS shall provide distribution amplifiers for the 10 MHz frequency reference and 1pps time reference signals. The distribution amplifiers shall accept the 10 MHz and 1pps signals at the DIFS external interfaces specified in Paragraphs 3.1.2.3.3.1 and Paragraph 3.1.2.3.3.2 and shall distribute the signals to all DIFS equipment requiring the reference signals at levels compatible with the DIFS equipment. DIFS Management Automation Software Suite (DMASS) The DMASS shall consist of one or more virtual machines resident on a virtualization host system provided by others as shown in Figure 3-2. The DMASS shall manage all DIFS equipment installed at the site and shall automate all tasks required to establish and maintain satellite communications DIFI paths traversing DIFS. Automation Functions The DMASS shall perform the following functions: Establish and terminate DIFI paths through DIFS based upon operator entered Satellite Access Agreement (SAA) parameters. Perform automatic protection switching for faulted DIFS equipment. Reroute DIFI paths through alternate facilities for faults and out-of-tolerance conditions that cannot be corrected locally. The current legacy analog infrastructure limits scalability, resilience, and interoperability. Under this Call for Solutions, the selected vendor will deliver, integrate, install, and acceptance-test a flexible, open-standard, modular Digital IF solution across up to twenty (20) worldwide satellite communications (SATCOM) teleport sites. Increment 1 will establish a fully operational baseline designed to support subsequent capability upgrades and integrations in future fiscal years. SECTION 2 – REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION PROBLEM STATEMENT Area of Interest: Modular Digital Intermediate Frequency Solu

quires an open-standard Digital IF architecture. However, before committing to a full-scale global deployment, the DoW must validate the operation, interoperability, security, and performance of these modular commercial solutions in a rigorous representative environment. Technical Objective & Scope The DoW seeks a commercial solution for an Increment 1 Digital IF capability set built on a flexible, open standard (e.g., Digital Intermediate Frequency Interoperability compliant), modular architecture. The selected solution will undergo standard site acceptance testing and operational verification to confirm compliance with contract performance requirements and site compatibility. Upon successful acceptance, this operational configuration will serve as the standardized baseline for deployment and installation across up to twenty (20) worldwide SATCOM teleport sites. Mission Impact Successful validation and deployment of this flexible open-standard Digital IF architecture will directly enhance warfighter lethality and survivability by delivering a highly resilient, agile, and survivable GEO-SATCOM capability which rapidly adapts to contested/congested environments. The current legacy analog infrastructure limits scalability, resilience, and interoperability. Under this Call for Solutions, the selected vendor will deliver, integrate, install, and acceptance-test a flexible, open-standard, modular Digital IF solution across up to twenty (20) worldwide satellite communications (SATCOM) teleport sites. Increment 1 will establish a fully operational baseline designed to support subsequent capability upgrades and integrations in future fiscal years. SECTION 2 – REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION PROBLEM STATEMENT Area of Interest: Modular Digital Intermediate Frequency Solu

quires an open-standard Digital IF architecture. However, before committing to a full-scale global deployment, the DoW must validate the operation, interoperability, security, and performance of these modular commercial solutions in a rigorous representative environment. Technical Objective & Scope The DoW seeks a commercial solution for an Increment 1 Digital IF capability set built on a flexible, open standard (e.g., Digital Intermediate Frequency Interoperability compliant), modular architecture. The selected solution will undergo standard site acceptance testing and operational verification to confirm compliance with contract performance requirements and site compatibility. Upon successful acceptance, this operational configuration will serve as the standardized baseline for deployment and installation across up to twenty (20) worldwide SATCOM teleport sites. Mission Impact Successful validation and deployment of this flexible open-standard Digital IF architecture will directly enhance warfighter lethality and survivability by delivering a highly resilient, agile, and survivable GEO-SATCOM capability which rapidly adapts to contested/congested environments. aintainable Design (Resilient): The commercial solution shall be designed for high availability Ai ≥ 0.9998) a long service life (15 years), and rapid maintainability (MTTR ≤ 30 minutes), using standard line-replaceable items (LRIs). All testing, data, and documentation produced shall support Wideband Global SATCOM (WGS) terminal certification. The Government will consider commercial solution approaches and vendors that fall along a spectrum of technological maturity, from capabilities that may require some further development to those that are fully commercialized and currently fielded. To meet these ESR bunch injection schemes and requirements, an array of stripline-based kickers, individually fed by high voltage (HV) pulse signals of up to +/-30 kV, will be installed in the ESR. The required deflection angle is in the range 1- 1.5 mrad, for the individual stripline kicker we target a deflection angle of ~125 µrad @ 18 GeV, assuming +/-27 kV pulse supply voltage between the kicker electrodes. To keep the losses of the stored beam low, a ~15 σ distance between the stored beam and the injection septa in the ESR must be maintained, which translates into a minimum physical aperture of 30 mm diameter for the stripline kickers. Competition is restricted to Krishagni LLC because NHLBI’s requirement is specifically to onboard to NEI’s active, Krishagni-licensed and operated OpenSpecimen environment rather than to procure a separate standalone biobanking system. Acquiring a different biobanking product would not satisfy the requirement to join the existing NEI shared instance and would result in substantial duplication of software licensing, implementation, validation, and support infrastructure costs, as well as unacceptable operational delays. As the software developer, proprietor, and operator of the existing NEI OpenSpecimen environment, Krishagni LLC is the only responsible source authorized and technically capable of performing the required onboarding, workflow configuration, and EMR integration services within that shared platform. The models must be scalable and efficient so that they can run at any interval up to once every 1 minute, as required by the end user. The archive results must not in any way affect the calculated data from its original resolution and sampled state. deadline_authority.rule: Only dates locally attached to tender/bid/quotation submission or requests-to-participate language can automatically resolve bid timing. Query/clarification dates are never accepted as submission deadlines. Missing/ambiguous submission evidence remains review-required before FINAL_SUPER_GREEN.

items.review_contract: Gate-ready authoritative DCE evidence pack from the current DCE generation. Unknown is never PASS. FINAL_SUPER_GREEN requires every mandatory gate resolved and authoritative deadline reconciliation.

ranking_contract: Recall-first discovery; post-DCE SPM-fit reranking only. Approximately 80% priority lane + 20% evidence-quality exploration lane. No candidate is declared eligible by this rank.
instruction: Review SPM_PRIORITY HOT/GOOD items first, then exploration. These are authoritative DCE evidence packs, not final verdicts. Unknown is never PASS.
